current_answer: As of 24 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. The clearest new movement is surface-scoped: OpenAI released GPT-6 Sol and Luna to Work, Codex, and the API but not ordinary Chat, while Work also had a resolved declared error incident; Claude recorded a resolved multi-model incident and then launched Opus 5.5. A community trace reports client and server model-attribution fields disagreeing, and conversation-capacity and allowance reports show real usable-work risk. These findings strengthen a surface, rollout, provenance, and budget diagnosis; they do not prove weaker model weights. Replay one fixed task with release boundary, requested and served model, request/server/native/client attribution, route, tools, context, budget, artifact, judge, and control before calling degradation.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: OpenAI changed Work before Chat. The new rollout, a resolved Work incident, and a model-label mismatch point to surface and provenance—not proof that popular model weights got worse.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven.
OpenAI says GPT-6 Sol and Luna entered Work, Codex, and the API but not ordinary Chat at launch; its release also warns that production Chat can differ from API or research evaluation.
OpenAI recorded a resolved ChatGPT Work error incident, while Claude recorded a resolved multi-model incident and current OpenAI, Claude, and xAI status pages were calm at the check.
A self-reported ChatGPT trace shows client and server model-attribution fields disagreeing; it is a provenance or display lead, not proof of fallback.
Early conversation-capacity and allowance reports show real usable-work risk around hidden tool/file work, but not weaker model weights.
Anthropic’s Opus 5.5 launch is a positive counterweight, although provider claims and mixed early user reports are not an independent time series.
Reader move: replay a fixed task across surfaces with release boundary, request/server/native/client/final model identity, route, tools, context, budget, artifact, judge, and control.
uncertainty: No matched fixed-task series across Chat, Work, Codex, API, and Claude with provider-served identity, route, tools, context, budget, artifact, judge, and representative denominator is available.
Provider status and release pages establish declared events and intended scope, not every account’s task quality or route.
The model-attribution mismatch is one self-reported client investigation and may be a UI or metadata defect.
Provider launch evaluations, community reports, and early counterreports use different tasks, plans, effort, and baselines.
Analytics, a human pilot, a provider ledger, a recovered-work measure, and willingness-to-pay evidence remain unavailable.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source research completed 24 September 2026. The broad call remains no capability decline proven; an official surface-scoped GPT-6 rollout, resolved Work and Claude incidents, a model-attribution mismatch, hidden capacity reports, and a positive Opus 5.5 counterweight sharpen the next replay.
